in_text_mentions: without transillumination defect or PS. The crystalline lens was clear, but the retrolental space appeared densely filled with cells and opacities. Funduscopic examination showed hazy media with a Weiss ring in the mid-vitreous cavity. The retina was attached, with no chorioretinal scars. The optic disc was not swollen, with a cup-to-disc ratio of about 0.5. The infrared image of the fundus reveals the central shadow of a detached vitreous body. B-scan ultrasonography confirmed the presence of a complete PVD with a shrunken vitreous body containing numerous fine echogenic opacities [Figure 1].

plate_findings.evidence: shadow of the partially detached vitreous body over the macula

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Left infrared fundus image in Fuchs Uveitis Syndrome article showing shadow of partially detached vitreous over macula, representing vitreous opacity/PVD manifestation described in caption. B: Right B-scan ultrasonography shows incomplete PVD with thickened peripheral vitreous cortex and echogenic opacities attributed to inflammatory cells in Fuchs Uveitis Syndrome; directly matches vitreous opacities vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Hedayatfar and Chee. Visual Blurring Following Posterior Vitreous Detachment in Fuchs Uveitis Syndrome.. Journal of ophthalmic & vision research 2026. doi:10.18502/jovr.v21.18382. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Left: The infrared image of the fundus reveals the shadow of the partially detached vitreous body over the macula. Right: B-scan ultrasonography (gain: 79 dB) demonstrates a detached vitreous body that retains attachments to the peripheral retina (incomplete PVD). The echogenic opacities are mainly confined to the thickened, irregular peripheral vitreous cortex (arrows). Note the echo-free space between the detached vitreous body and the retina (asterisk).
in_text_mentions: mal, and OCT showed no macular edema. Direct funduscopy using a 90-diopter lens revealed a detached posterior hyaloid face. B-scan ultrasonography demonstrated an incomplete PVD, with a thickened peripheral vitreous cortex contributing significantly to the echogenic opacity. This might imply the accumulation of inflammatory cells, opacities, and condensed vitreous strands on the peripheral vitreous cortex [Figure 2]. Three months later, she continued to experience unstable, blurred vision and disturbing floaters. Due to the lack of improvement, PPV was performed, restoring the vision to 20/20.

plate_findings.evidence: hypofluorescent amoeboid shadow of the detached vitreous body

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Left FA panel is real patient ophthalmic image in Fuchs Uveitis Syndrome article; hypofluorescent amoeboid shadow represents detached vitreous body with opacities obscuring posterior pole fluorescence, attributed to Fuchs disease by caption and title. B: Right B-scan is real patient ultrasound image in Fuchs Uveitis Syndrome case showing numerous fine reflective opacities within detached vitreous gel, directly matching vitreous cells and opacities vocabulary term.
panels.attribution_text: Hedayatfar and Chee. Visual Blurring Following Posterior Vitreous Detachment in Fuchs Uveitis Syndrome.. Journal of ophthalmic & vision research 2026. doi:10.18502/jovr.v21.18382. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Left: Fluorescein angiography during the arteriovenous phase shows a hot disc and hypofluorescent amoeboid shadow of the detached vitreous body. Right: B-scan ultrasonography (gain: 90 dB) shows the detached vitreous gel encompassing numerous fine reflective opacities and a thickened echogenic membrane in the peripheral vitreous compartment (arrow).
in_text_mentions: B-scan ultrasonography revealed an incomplete PVD with numerous fine reflective opacities within the vitreous gel as well as a thick echogenic membrane lining the peripheral vitreous body. FA showed a hot disc without any perivascular or macular leakage. A large, indistinct, amoeboid hypofluorescent shadow obscured the typical fluorescence of the posterior pole [Figure 3]. OCT confirmed the absence of CME.

plate_findings.evidence: Iris Koeppe's nodule of a 39-year-old male patient (A)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Slit-lamp photograph of a CMV-associated Fuchs uveitis syndrome (FUS) patient showing an iris Koeppe's nodule at the pupillary border; Koeppe iris nodules are a classic, hallmark manifestation of Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis, so the configured disease attribution is clear. Patient is a 39-year-old male (adult). No skin, no stated ethnicity in caption or in-text. B: Slit-lamp photograph of a CMV-associated Fuchs uveitis syndrome (FUS) patient showing coin-shaped keratic precipitates on the corneal endothelium. Keratic precipitates are a defining feature of Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis, supporting the configured disease attribution; the exact 'coin-shaped' morphology is named in the caption but is not present in the allowed vocabulary (only stellate and diffuse KP entries exist), so it is recorded in proposed_findings rather than forcing an incorrect vocabulary key.
